name: Origin Protocol
rootCause: Origin Dollar (OUSD) was exploited for over $7 million on November 17, 2020, when a reentrancy vulnerability in its vault contract allowed an attacker to inflate their OUSD balance using a malicious token and a flash loan. The bug stemmed from a missing validation check that had been mistakenly removed during refactoring, leaving the contract exposed. A validation check preventing reentrancy was accidentally removed from the OUSD vault contract during a refactor, enabling external ERC-20 token contracts to reenter the vault via callback before vault accounting was updated.

descriptions.text: Stay at home, wear a mask, the hack epidemic is spreading.These are dark times for weak code. Developers need to put their protocols into lockdown. Greed is contagious, and hacks bring eye-catching prizes. In just 24 hours we hear of two more attacks.

Origin Dollar (OUSD) was exploited for over $7 million on November 17, 2020, when a reentrancy vulnerability in its vault contract allowed an attacker to inflate their OUSD balance using a malicious token and a flash loan. The bug stemmed from a missing validation check that had been mistakenly removed during refactoring, leaving the contract exposed. A validation check preventing reentrancy was accidentally removed from the OUSD vault contract during a refactor, enabling external ERC-20 token contracts to reenter the vault via callback before vault accounting was updated.
